rationale: C21 is the immediately preceding annual Flag Day proclamation and plausibly supplied both the structure and material language of the 1951 proclamation: the congressional joint-resolution predicate, the historical reference to the Continental Congress's adoption of the flag on June 14, 1777, the direction to display the flag on public buildings, and the call for public ceremonies honoring the emblem. C24 and C18 are also strong members of the same recurring drafting lineage, but C21 is the closest prior annual template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved on August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), has set aside June 14 of each year as Flag Day
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Congress, by a joint resolution approved August 3, 1949 (63 Stat. 492), has designated June 14 of each year as Flag Day
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim statement of the same statutory basis.

shared_material.child_excerpt: in commemoration of the adoption of the flag of the United States by the Continental Congress on June 14, 1777
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the anniversary of the adoption on June 14, 1777, by the Continental Congress, of the Stars and Stripes as the official flag of the United States of America
shared_material.explanation: The same historical predicate is retained with minor compression.

shared_material.child_excerpt: direct that the flag of the United States be displayed on all Government buildings on Flag Day ... and I call upon the people to observe that day with special patriotic ceremonies
shared_material.parent_excerpt: call upon the appropriate officials ... to arrange for the display of the flag ... on all public buildings on Flag Day ... and I urge the people ... to observe that day ... by participating in ceremonies especially designed to honor our national emblem
shared_material.explanation: Parallel operative sequence: government-building flag display followed by a public call for commemorative ceremonies.
